summary.text: An elliptical galaxy has an approximately ellipsoidal shape and a smooth, nearly featureless image.
Most are made of older, low-mass stars with a sparse interstellar medium, so star formation is typically minimal.
They range from dwarfs with tens of millions of stars to supergiants of over one hundred trillion, and make up roughly 10 to 15% of galaxies in the Virgo Supercluster.

facts.label: Share of galaxies
facts.value: About 10 to 15% in the Virgo Supercluster

facts.label: Where found
facts.value: Close to the centers of galaxy clusters

facts.label: Black holes
facts.value: Every massive one has a supermassive black hole

facts.label: Famous example
facts.value: M87, whose black hole was the first one imaged

items.prompt: Elliptical galaxies look red rather than blue. What does that say about their stars?

options.label: Old stars dominate, with few young ones
Young, hot stars dominate but sit behind gas
A thick layer of dust reddens their light
Their stars are mostly new and still forming

items.explain: Ellipticals have little interstellar matter and few young stars, and their old stellar populations give them red colors.

items.prompt: A quiet elliptical galaxy suddenly shows a brief burst of new stars. What event is the likely cause?

options.label: Its spiral arms winding up
A merger with another galaxy
Its central black hole running out of mass
Its stars reaching old age

items.explain: Star formation in ellipticals is typically minimal, though they may undergo brief periods of it when merging with other galaxies.

items.prompt: Early on, Edwin Hubble guessed that one kind of galaxy turned into another over time. Which guess did later work show to be false?

options.label: That spirals evolve into ellipticals
That irregulars evolve into spirals
That ellipticals evolve into spirals
That ellipticals evolve into irregulars

items.explain: Hubble hypothesized that ellipticals evolved into spirals, which was later discovered to be false.

items.prompt: A galaxy looks perfectly round in the sky. Why might it still be elongated?

options.label: How it looks depends on viewing angle and true shape
Round-looking galaxies are always elongated ones
Its thick dust makes it look rounder than it is
Telescopes always make every galaxy look rounder

items.explain: Hubble's shape classification depends on both the galaxy's intrinsic shape and the angle it is viewed from, so some E0 galaxies are actually elongated.

items.prompt: Compare the stars of a flat spiral galaxy with those of an elliptical. How do the elliptical's stars move?

options.label: In orderly circles within one thin plane
In clean paths along a pair of spiral arms
In somewhat random orbits around the center, in three dimensions
In straight lines out of the galaxy

items.explain: Ellipticals are more three-dimensional and unstructured, with stars in somewhat random orbits around the center.

items.prompt: Which property of an elliptical galaxy's stars is tied to the mass of its central black hole?

options.label: How red their color is
How many globular clusters surround them
How widely their velocities vary
How many of them are young

items.explain: The M-sigma relation links the velocity dispersion of the surrounding stars to the mass of the black hole at the center.
